newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says NZ confident it can deliver surpluses.
newsitem.headline: Peters says NZ confident it can deliver surpluses.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday he believed careful fiscal management would ensure the country produced forecast budget surpluses in coming years despite current lower than expected growth rates.

Speaking to Reuters Financial Television in Sydney, and monitored in Wellington, Peters said "We are very confident...if we are very careful in the fiscal management of New Zealand's economy, (and) if we are very, very careful about government expenditure and ensure that we get value for money, and that we only spend money where there is value, I think we can deliver those surpluses and deliver the other social policies as well."

Peters reiterated that the aim of generating surpluses would be to make it possible to repay debt and bring it down to a net proportion of GDP "of just round about 20 percent by the end of the century".
He added that this view of an economic recovery out of its current growth trough was based on forecasts he believed were well-balanced.
"We have forecast (GDP) growth for the 1998/99 year to be at about 4.0, 4.2 percent -- now I think that's a fairly medium forecast.
"We may do better than that, we may do slightly worse than that, but its a pretty good range to be looking at coming off a growth rate of about 2.2 (in 1997/98)," he said.
After the June budget many economists were critical of what they saw as the optimistic undertone of both Treasury's growth forecasts and the government's expectations of continued surpluses.
